title: Create a Session Bar Chart
constraints: duration is a non-negative number of seconds and never null
reference:
WITH labeled AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN duration < 300 THEN '[0-5>'
      WHEN duration < 600 THEN '[5-10>'
      WHEN duration < 900 THEN '[10-15>'
      ELSE '15 or more'
    END AS bin
  FROM Sessions
),
bins AS (
  SELECT '[0-5>' AS bin
  UNION ALL SELECT '[5-10>'
  UNION ALL SELECT '[10-15>'
  UNION ALL SELECT '15 or more'
)
SELECT b.bin, COUNT(l.bin) AS total
FROM bins AS b
LEFT JOIN labeled AS l
  ON l.bin = b.bin
GROUP BY b.bin;
brute:
SELECT '[0-5>' AS bin, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Sessions WHERE duration / 60 < 5) AS total
UNION ALL
SELECT '[5-10>', (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Sessions WHERE duration / 60 >= 5 AND duration / 60 < 10)
UNION ALL
SELECT '[10-15>', (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Sessions WHERE duration / 60 >= 10 AND duration / 60 < 15)
UNION ALL
SELECT '15 or more', (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Sessions WHERE duration / 60 >= 15)
notes:
## Intuition

Two separate jobs hide here. First, every session must be put in exactly one bin, which is a `CASE` over the duration in seconds (5, 10 and 15 minutes are 300, 600 and 900 seconds). Second, the chart needs **all four** bins, even empty ones. Grouping the sessions alone can only produce bins that contain a session, so the four labels have to come from a small table of their own, and the sessions are counted against it with a left join.

## Approach

1. CTE `labeled`: one row per session holding its `bin` label. The `CASE` tests the upper bounds in increasing order, so the first true branch is the right bin.
2. CTE `bins`: the four labels, written as a `UNION ALL` of constant rows.
3. `LEFT JOIN` `labeled` (alias `l`) to `bins` (alias `b`) on the label, so a bin with no sessions still yields one row whose `l.bin` is `null`.
4. `GROUP BY b.bin` and report `COUNT(l.bin)` as `total`. `COUNT` of a column skips nulls, so an empty bin counts 0.

## Example 1, step by step

`labeled` turns the durations 30, 199, 299, 580 and 1000 into `[0-5>`, `[0-5>`, `[0-5>`, `[5-10>` and `15 or more`. Joining with `bins`:

| b.bin | matching l.bin rows | total |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[0-5>` | 3 | 3 |
| `[5-10>` | 1 | 1 |
| `[10-15>` | none (one row with null) | 0 |
| `15 or more` | 1 | 1 |

## Complexity

- Time: O(N) to label N sessions, plus a join against four bins.
- Space: O(N) for `labeled`.

## Pitfalls

- `GROUP BY` the `CASE` alone silently omits bins with no sessions, such as `[10-15>` in the example.
- `COUNT(*)` after the left join counts the null row of an empty bin as 1; count `l.bin` instead.
- Boundaries are half-open: 300 seconds is already `[5-10>` and 900 seconds is `15 or more`. Using `<=` moves sessions of exactly 5, 10 or 15 minutes into the wrong bin.
- The labels must match character for character, including the `>` and the spaces in `15 or more`.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `labeled` | each session reduced to its bin label |
| `bins` | the four labels, so empty bins still exist |
| `b` / `l` | a bin and the labeled sessions that fall into it |
| `COUNT(l.bin)` | sessions in the bin, 0 when only the null row joined |

narration.1: The labeled stage gives every session its bin.
narration.4: Under 300 seconds is under 5 minutes; the branches are tried in order, so later ones only see longer sessions.
narration.11: The bins stage lists all four labels so that empty bins are not lost.

narration.18: Start from the bins, the side whose rows must all appear.
narration.19: A left join keeps a bin even when no session carries its label.
